Press Release:


Zuma: the final straw?
He was invited to give the key-note speech at one of the ANC’s tripartite alliance partners’ Workers day rallies in the Free State. But instead, embattled
President Jacob Zuma was forced to abandon his moment in the spotlight. Booed, heckled and whisked away in his motorcade, workers attending the Cosatu
rally rejected him, demanding that he step down as the country’s commander in chief. As the pressure mounts, Carte Blanche asks: what’s really keeping
Zuma in power?

Script:


Despite media reports and statements by politicians to the contrary, many would argue that on Monday the voice of the workers ruled the day. In Bloemfontein fighting and boo'ing of President Zuma caused the speeches to be cancelled – the first time a president of the ANC was prevented from speaking at an alliance rally.

Upsound
The day is cancelled

It was also the first time that Zuma was boo'ed outside Gauteng. At three of the other rallies, senior ANC members seen as pro-zuma were also boo'ed and prevented from speaking. Political analyst Karima Brown
Karima
I think it was a seminal moment for Pres Jacob Zuma's presidency of the ANC, his leadership of the tripartite alliance ae well as president of the country. As you know Pres JZ has dismissed previous calls for him to step down and of course marches by ordinary South Africans from all political persuasions as people who are racists and those who want to hold on to their privilege. What we saw on May day in Manaung was a rejection by the very base which JZ claims to represent – black working class people – and of course more importantly workers allied to the ANC in the Alliance under Cosatu.



In 1885 a working class uprising in Chicago lead to Mayday becoming the international day for workers, and on the centenary of the Red Revolution in Russia, Former ANC Treasurer General dr Mathews Phosa says the day is still significant
Dr Mathews Phosa
Workers day is a world event. And it was important that the trade union movement in this country, Cosatu, should observe the day with all our support. It's very important.

Since 1994,he ANC has remained in power largely with the support of the workers, through the SA Communist Party and the Congress of South African Trade Unions, or Cosatu - together known as the tripartite alliance.

This year on May Day, Cosatu planned a series of marches to hand over lists of grievances on behalf of its members
Cosatu
We took a decision last year in our central executive committee that going forward from last year May days, going forward we're going to celebrate our May day's in the form of a march.

But recent events, and especially the controversial cabinet reshuffle by president Jacob Zuma increased tensions between the alliance partners -with both Cosatu and the SACP for the first time publicly asking for Zuma to go. Solly Mapaila is the 2nd Deputy general Secretary of the SACP
SACP
The president has committed gross errors. He must leave. He has abdicated his responsibility as president, handed over the presidency and the independence of this country to the Guptas. That's sufficient enough to remove him from office. Let alone the previous scandals that he has.
Link bongani
(Politics is all about perception and what is an alliance but a show of force.) Like the SACP, Cosatu has also called for Pres Zuma to step down but they want to make it clear that their fight is not with the party but with the man in charge.
Cosatu
Remember Pres Zuma is not the alliance alone. We are in alliance with the ANC, we're not in alliance with individuals. So if we call for the president of the ANC to step down or the president of the republic to step down it does not suggest we are breaking the alliance.

Last week some of the biggest member unions asked Cosatu not to allow the South African president to speak at the the main event in Bloemfontein
Cosatu
(There was a meeting between Cosatu and the ANC.) Cosatu made it very clear tot he ANC that there's no guarantee that Pres Zuma would not be boo'ed and those things because as Cosatu we have not planned that thing.

But, using a technicality, (that Jacob Zuma would attend as president of the ANC and not as president of South Africa,) the ANC made it clear that the president would be there.
ANC
You must remember there is no Cosatu decision that the president of the ANC must not attend or address any activity. The decision is about the president of the republic. The view is expressed by one or two Cosatu affiliates and that view you could not find expression. When we met with Cosatu the Friday before Monday May Day event they were still assured that their decision has got nothing to do with the president of the ANC, just got everything to do with the president of the republic.

Pre-empting a possible hostile reception, Phetoe says the ANC started filling up the the stadium with Zuma supporters while the cosatu members were still marching.
Cosatu
The challenge came when workers realised that the Freestate ANC printed T-shirts – 100% support zuma – and workers thought this is a provoke on the base of the decision that Cosatu has taken against Jacob Zuma to step down.

The two groups started fighting, and the crowd bayed for Zuma to go.

The president was rushed off in his motorcade Prof Tinyiko Maluleke says what’s at stake is more than just the unity of the alliance
Prof Maluleke
We are dealing with a fracturing of the glue that held not just the aliance partners together, but the glue that held society together. Because the president is a symbol of all of us, of our unity, and for him to be boo'ed in the manner that it happened, I think for me it's quite worrysome.

But speaking at the WEF two days later, President Zuma seemed unperturbed.
JZ
I've been hearing comments all over. The problem is that people have not understood what democracy is all about. You will agree with me that in the countries of dictators there will be no protests, there will be no boo'ing. Protests, boo-ing, debates is part of the culture of democracy.
Maluleke
To be fair to Pres JZ he has never, he has never lied to us in so far as his desire to stay in power is concerned. He has always been very clear that he's going nowhere.
Karima
Pres JZ is a big tree. Uprooting him is not going to be an event. It's a process and there is a full-scale revolt inside the ANC, inside the alliance an also in society. He is being stretched on simply every single front.

The ANC is organising discussions to patch up the alliance, but the SACP has made it clear that Jacob Zuma is not welcome at their congress in July, and that they will mobilise the masses until he goes. Even December is too far away
Solly
This country can't afford 7 months with Pres Zuma in charge. It's too long. The pain of our people losing confidence on our liberation movement, on the history that many of our Mathias died fighting for, on the history of sacrifices of people like Pres Nelson Mandela, Oliver Thambo, Walter Sisulu, Chris Hani, Joe Slovo and many others – the pain of going through that on a daily basis is so unacceptable. I think that the ANC have to protect it's own history amd this president perhaps now we can realise it was a huge mistake for him to ascend to that particular position.

(Dr Phosa feels he should go, but with a dignified exit)
But in the end it's the ANC's decision, and for now, their opinion remains divided
Phosa


But even though some ANC members want him out, he still has the official support
Zizi
Pres Zuma has got unwaivering support of members of the ANC as the current president of the ANC. Like all presidents of the ANC before there could be observations about the manner of his leadership, it does not mean he does not enjoy support of the leadership.
Maluleke
If the ANC takes back it's role as leader, I think it is possible we could see change of direction. If not the ANC has got only itself to blame because come 2019 the ANC might lose power.
Solly
He can walk away and save our movement and our revolution. He's not willing to. He can see it. I think ultimately I can say he's a coward. I used to think he's a brave man who fought for our liberation but I now know he's a coward. He's willing to die with his own people, with his own children as the father of this country.
Matthew
We've got one country, one national flag, one national anthem and one future. We dare not mess up any of them


Promo 1: 15sec
The ANC, and the country is divided over Pres Jacob Zuma, and after Monday’s May day chaos, how much more can he survive?

SACP - I used to think he was a brave man - he’s a coward...



Promo 2: 15sec
Maluleke :
"If the Anc takes back it’s role as leader we could see a change of direction”
v/o

Booed by workers – how much more pressure can President Zuma withstand?
